newsitem.title: LEBANON: Malaysian firms buy prime Beirut real estate.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian firms buy prime Beirut real estate.

text.p: Five Malaysian companies have signed a contract to buy 8,000 square metres of prime seafront in central Beirut for a $75 million tourism development, the Solidere real estate company said on Wednesday.
Sources close to the deal said the land, on a choice plot overlooking a park beside the St Georges bay next to the Lebanese capital's hotels district, cost $25 million.

An executive of Solidere, which is rebuilding the Beirut Central District, told Reuters the deal would open up the reconstruction of the capital to Asian companies and in particular, to Malaysian companies.

"It's a very nice plot in a very strategic position, something really nice. These are five listed companies on the Malaysian stock exchange with experience in the tourism area so, they are substantial companies," Mounib Mounib Hammoud, Solidere exective responsible for strategy and marketing said.
The development will total 24,000 square metres of built-up area.
It is the first non-Arab investment in central Beirut that Solidere began rebuilding in 1994 under a 25-year programme.
"Solidere signed on Tuesday a contract to sell 8,000 square metres to a group of Malaysian businessmen accompanying Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad," a Solidere statement said.

"The buyer is Premier Equity, which includes several prominent Malaysian companies as shareholders. The contract permits the construction of a touristic-residential project, including a five-star hotel," the statement said.
The total cost of the project was expected to exceed $75 million and would be completed by the year 2,000, it added.
The five Malaysian companies were named as Berjaya Vacation Club Berhad, Dijaya Corporation Berhad, Transwater Corporation Berhad, MWE Holdings Berhad and Penas Holdings Sdn. Bhd.
Non-Arabs buying Lebanese real estate is restricted, and they are not allowed to buy Solidere shares as a result.

An industry source said Premier Equity was a Cayman Islands company set up for the purpose and under Lebanese law it would either have to apply to the Lebanese government for approval of the purchase or set up a Lebanese company with Lebanese partners.
A Lebanese company with a majority of non-Arab shareholders is allowed to own up to 10,000 square metres of land in the capital, a source said.
Mahathir, who began on Monday a three-day official visit to Lebanon to promote Malaysian investment in Lebanon, is accompanied by more than 30 private sector representatives.
